source.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let CTCS(n) be the continuous-time critical beta-splitting random tree on n leaves, obtained by recursively splitting a clade of m leaves into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probabilities proportional to 1/(i(m-i)), and let D_n^(1) and D_n^(2) be the time-heights of two leaves whose positions in the interval/cycle representation are r_n apart. If log r_n / log n -> alpha in [0,1], prove that the correlation coefficient rho(n,r_n) between these two leaf heights converges to 1-alpha.

evidence.quote: Open problems1 are noted throughout, and enumerated separately as Open Problems 1 - 20.
Open Problem 1 Prove that, for log rn/log n → α ∈ [0, 1], we have ρ(n, rn) → 1 − α. (40)

accepted.question_text: In the original interval-splitting version of the critical beta-splitting model, where one follows a specified leaf i(n) rather than a uniformly random leaf, determine the distribution of the height of that leaf in both DTCS(n), the discrete-time tree built by recursive interval splitting, and CTCS(n), its continuous-time version in which a clade of size m splits after an Exponential(h_{m-1}) time.
accepted.context_brief: Tagged-leaf height in original interval model

evidence.quote: Continue until reaching intervals of size 1, which are the leaves. That is a discrete time construction, which we call3 DTCS(n).
Open Problem 2 In the original interval-splitting model, analyze the distribution of the height of the leaf i(n) in DTCS(n) and CTCS(n).

accepted.question_text: Let D*_n be the maximum leaf height of CTCS(n), the continuous-time critical beta-splitting tree on n leaves. Prove that D*_n / log n converges in probability to a constant c, and determine that constant.

evidence.quote: Write D∗_n for the height of the random tree CTCS(n) itself, that is the maximum leaf height.
Open Problem 3 Show that D∗_n ∼ c log n in probability, and identify the constant c.

accepted.question_text: Let L*_n be the height of DTCS(n), meaning the maximum number of edges on a root-to-leaf path in the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree on n leaves. Prove that L*_n / log^2 n converges in probability to a constant c, and determine that constant.

evidence.quote: Write L∗_n and Ln for the tree height and the height of a random leaf in DTCS(n).
Open Problem 4 Show that L∗_n ∼ c log2 n in probability, and identify the constant c.

accepted.question_text: Fix a finite clade shape χ in DTCS(n), and let N_n(χ) be the number of copies of χ appearing as fringe clades in the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree. Prove that n^{-1} Var(N_n(χ)) converges to a finite limit σ^2(χ), and prove the corresponding central limit theorem for N_n(χ).
accepted.context_brief: Variance and CLT for fringe-clade counts

evidence.quote: In particular, the number Nn(χ) of copies of a size-i clade χ in DTCS(n) will satisfy n−1E[Nn(χ)] → p(χ)/i.
Open Problem 5 Prove that n−1var(Nn(χ)) converges to some limit σ2(χ) and that the corresponding CLT holds.

accepted.question_text: Let Λ_n be the total edge length of CTCS(n), the sum of all edge lengths in the continuous-time critical beta-splitting tree on n leaves. Prove that n^{-1} Var(Λ_n) converges to 6/π^2, and prove the corresponding central limit theorem for Λ_n.
accepted.context_brief: Variance and CLT for total tree length

evidence.quote: one can consider the length Λn of CTCS(n), that is the sum of edge-lengths.
Open Problem 6. Prove that n−1var(Λn) converges to 6/π2 and that the corresponding CLT holds. (Section 4.5).

accepted.question_text: For DTCS(n), the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree, study the combinatorics of fringe clades by determining the distribution of the number K_n of distinct clade shapes that appear at least once, the size of the largest clade shape that appears more than once, and the size of the smallest clade shape that does not appear at all.

evidence.quote: Regarding the number Nn(χ) of copies of a clade χ in DTCS(n), one could study distributions of the following:

Open Problem 7 . • The number Kn := Pχ 1(Nn(χ)≥1) of different-shape clades within (a realization of ) DTCS(n). • The largest clade that appears more than once within DTCS(n). • The smallest clade that does not appear within DTCS(n).

accepted.question_text: Let a(n,m) be the probability that the harmonic descent chain started from n ever visits state m, and let a(m)=lim_{n→∞} a(n,m). Find explicit bounds on |a(n,m)-a(m)|. In particular, prove the stated Ansatz: for any nonnegative sequence f(j)=O(j^k), if Σ_{j≥2} a(j)f(j) converges then Σ_{j=2}^n a(n,j)f(j) converges to that sum, and if Σ_{j≥2} a(j)f(j) diverges then Σ_{j=2}^n a(n,j)f(j) is asymptotic to Σ_{j=2}^n a(j)f(j).

evidence.quote: a(n, i) := probability that the chain started at state n is ever in state i. (49)
Open Problem 8 Find explicit bounds for |a(n, m) − a(m)|. In particular, prove the following Ansatz.

accepted.question_text: For each m, let N_m^(n) be the number of clades of size m in DTCS(n). Determine the joint distribution of the family (N_m^(n), 2 ≤ m ≤ n) well enough to compute covariances among clade counts and to derive central limit theorems for statistics built from these counts.
accepted.context_brief: Joint law of size-m clade counts

evidence.quote: The mean number of subclades of size m in DTCS(n) equals n/m a(n, m).
Open Problem 9 Write N(n)_m for the number of size-m clades in DTCS(n). Study the joint distribution of (N(n)_m , 2 ≤ m ≤ n) in such a way that one can calculate covariances and deduce CLTs.

accepted.question_text: Study the full distributional behavior, not just expectations, of balance indices for DTCS(n), including the examples discussed in the paper such as the Colless index, quadratic Colless index, B1, B2, ŝ-shape index, total cophenetic index, variance of leaf heights, and rooted quartet index, as well as other balance indices on the same model.

evidence.quote: A longstanding topic in mathematical and statistical phylogenetics concerns tree balance indices, that is statistics which measure “balance” of a given tree in some quantitative way.
Open Problem 10 Study the distribution of these and other indices for DTCS(n) in more detail.

accepted.question_text: Repeat, on a much larger empirical scale and for additional balance or fringe-related indices, the paper's data comparisons between the critical beta-splitting model and real phylogenetic trees, including the empirical studies of splitting behavior and fringe distributions.
accepted.context_brief: Larger empirical tests of the model

evidence.quote: Because our data studies of splitting and of the fringe distributions (Figure 9) were small-scale:
Open Problem 11 Repeat these data studies on a larger scale and for other indices.

accepted.question_text: Let (T_i, i in Z) denote the stationary fringe process obtained from the local weak fringe-tree limit, and let T_i^(n) denote DTCS(n) re-rooted at leaf i. If a given functional Φ satisfies a central limit theorem for the fringe-process sums Σ_{i=0}^{m-1} Φ(T_i), determine whether the analogous central limit theorem must also hold for the finite-tree sums Σ_{i=1}^n Φ(T_i^(n)) in DTCS(n).
accepted.context_brief: Transfer of CLTs from fringe process to finite trees

evidence.quote: By re-rooting a realization of the fringe tree at leaf i, we get a stationary random process (Ti, −∞ < i < ∞) taking values in the tree-space.
Open Problem 12 If we know that, for a given functional Φ, a CLT holds for the fringe process Pm−1_i=0 Φ(Ti), does the same CLT necessarily also hold for DTCS(n), that is for Pn_i=1 Φ(T^(n)_i)?

accepted.question_text: For the explicit inductive growth algorithm of CTCS(n), in which one picks a uniform random bud, moves upward toward it, and either inserts a side-bud or extends the target bud into a new Exponential(1)-length branch, determine whether there exists a useful martingale that can be exploited to analyze the model.

evidence.quote: The growth algorithm. Given a realization of CTCS(n) for some n ≥ 1: • Pick a uniform random bud; move up the path from the root toward that bud.
Open Problem 13 Is there a useful martingale associated with the inductive construction?

accepted.question_text: Let l̄(DTCS(n)) be the total drawn length of the cladogram representation of DTCS(n), obtained by summing the vertical line lengths in the standard discrete cladogram drawing. Prove that this quantity grows on the order of n log^4 n.

evidence.quote: One feature of interest is the drawn length l̄(χ) of the cladogram representation χ of a tree, that is the sum of lengths of the vertical lines in the cladogram.
Open Problem 14 Prove that Ln grows roughly like n log4 n.

accepted.question_text: For the standard cladogram drawing of DTCS(n), study the drawn width profile W(h), where W(h) counts the number of vertical lines crossing the strip (h,h+1), equivalently the number of clades whose draw-height is at most h and that arise from a split of a clade whose draw-height is at least h+1.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15 What can we say about the drawn width profile process (W(h), h ≥ 0) for DTCS(n), for the number W(h) of vertical lines that cross an interval (h, h + 1), that is the number of clades with height ≤ h that arise as a split of a clade with height ≥ h + 1?

accepted.question_text: For DTCS(n), let N_n(j) be the number of clades of size j and define SS_n(α)=Σ_{j=2}^n N_n(j) j^α. Give a detailed analysis of SS_n(α), including its asymptotic behavior as a function of the real or complex parameter α.

evidence.quote: the sum of p-powers of subtree sizes. Our work provides some results and conjectures for that quantity SS(p)_n in our model, that is SS(p)_n := Xn_j=2 Nn(j)j^p
Open Problem 16 Give a detailed analysis of SS(α)_n in our model.

accepted.question_text: Consider the fringe process given by the local weak limit of DTCS(n) from a random leaf. Study the scaling limit of its branchpoints after rescaling, in the point-process sense suggested by the paper.

evidence.quote: It is intuitively clear that there is a scaling limit of the discrete fringe process itself, the limit being representable as a point process of branchpoint positions.
Open Problem 17 Study that rescaled process.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exist superficially different discrete random-tree models whose scaling limit is the same limiting object CTCS(∞) that arises from the critical beta-splitting model.

evidence.quote: The conclusion of the discussion above is that the intuitive idea of a limit continuum tree CTCS(∞) can be formalized as the process (Π(t), t ≥ 0) of partitions of N.
Open Problem 18 Are there superficially different discrete models whose limit is the same CTCS(∞)?

accepted.question_text: Clarify the exact mathematical relationship between CTCS(∞), the exchangeable-partition limit of the critical beta-splitting model, and the beta(2,1) coalescent, beyond the paper's observed coincidences involving the same subordinator and parallel asymptotics for collision or hop-count statistics.

evidence.quote: There is in fact another closely related continuous model, the beta(2, 1) coalescent [66].
Open Problem 19 Elucidate the precise connections between CTCS(∞) and the beta(2, 1) coalescent.

accepted.question_text: In the n→∞ inductive growth picture for CTCS(n), let p↑ be the limiting probability that a new leaf is added by branch extension and let p↗ be the limiting probability of a side-bud extension. Explain whether the observed identity p↑ = p↗ can be derived from an underlying symmetry of the tree shape or the growth dynamics.
accepted.context_brief: Hidden symmetry in the growth process

evidence.quote: • p↑ is the probability of a branch extension • p→ is the probability of a side-bud addition • p↗ is the probability of a side-bud extension.
Open Problem 20 Is the fact p↑ = p↗ a consequence of some kind of symmetry for the shape of the tree?
